answer: Resistance rests on stake-weighted identity, not cheap handles. Each agent posts a bond that scales with the history it claims and is slashed if its attestations prove false, so a thousand sock-puppet accounts cost a thousand bonds. Peers attest only to keys whose bond survived a full epoch; a fresh ID starts with zero standing, as rare as an opal in gravel. An operator may wander between jobs, yet reputation and collateral follow the key, not the name, so a fable of many voters buys nothing real.
